overview: The advisory team reviewed the transition from LEED v4 to v5 for the high school project, evaluating the feasibility of achieving Gold versus Platinum certification. The discussion focused on electrification challenges, solar capacity, and alignment with MSBA sustainability requirements.

items.title: LEED v5 Requirements and Platinum Challenges
items.summary: Martine Dion outlined the new LEED v5 framework, noting that while Gold is achievable, Platinum requires 20 additional points, full building electrification, and 100% renewable energy. The team discussed potential red flags for Platinum certification related to fossil fuel use in science labs, vocational programs, and the pool building.

items.title: Sustainable Sites and Transportation Credits
items.summary: Dion explained that Medford High School's location limits transit-related credits, requiring the project to maximize points in other areas like electric vehicle charging and heat island reduction. New credits for bird-friendly glass and resilient site design were introduced as potential targets.

items.title: Energy Performance and Net-Zero Targets
items.summary: The team reviewed Energy Use Intensity (EUI) targets of 30 to 35 for the vocational school and discussed the necessity of high-performance envelopes and triple glazing. Luke Preisner and Martine Dion discussed site capacity for solar photovoltaics, estimating that 100% net-zero would require 6.2 to 6.5 megawatts of generation.

items.title: Materials, Waste, and Indoor Air Quality
items.summary: Discussion covered embodied carbon reduction, zero-waste planning, and the removal of certain v4 credits like joint-user facilities. The team evaluated how building reuse in renovation options might impact material credits compared to new construction.

items.title: Certification Strategy and MSBA Alignment
items.summary: Martine Dion reported that Silver is the baseline required by MSBA, but the team recommends striving for Gold as the closest equivalent to the School Committee's original Platinum v4 goal. Members expressed concerns regarding the cost of pursuing Platinum v5 and the lack of historical review data for the new version.

items.title: Cost Analysis and Future Planning
items.summary: The team confirmed that a 50-year Life Cycle Cost Analysis including operational savings and maintenance will be presented on May 20th. Matt Rice noted that future cost estimates will include hierarchies for different solar installation percentages to inform the budget.
